exercises.title: Insert and look up
exercises.task: Fill the three holes: Insert goes down one letter at a time, creating the missing children, and marks the last node as the end of a word; find follows the letters and gives up (returns nil) as soon as a letter is missing. Contains and HasPrefix are written for you on top of find.
hints: In Insert: next, ok := node.children[r]; if it is missing, create it with NewTrie() and store it; then node = next.
After the loop, node is where the word ends: node.word = true.
In find, the same lookup, but return nil when the child is missing.

exercises.title: Autocomplete
exercises.task: Write the body of walk in Complete: every word below the prefix's node, in alphabetical order. A map has no order, so sort the letters of the children before visiting them. Run completes Go's keywords and predeclared names, the way your editor does.
hints: It is a depth-first walk (A9): visit the node itself, then each child.
Collect the keys of node.children into a []rune, sort it, then call walk(node.children[r], word+string(r)) for each.
